items.title: 2 dead after car found crashed into tree in Miami-Dade, deputies said
items.text:
The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Two people were killed after a crash in Miami-Dade County on Sunday, deputies said.
According to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office, at around 1:15 a.m., deputies arrived in the area of Southwest Eighth Street and 43rd Avenue after receiving reports of a crash.
At the scene, deputies found a vehicle that had struck a tree, and fire rescue pronounced a man and a woman dead.
items.desc: Two people were killed after a crash in Miami-Dade County on Sunday, deputies said.

items.title: ‘They are like dangerous dogs’: Man shares frustration after reported dog bite in NW Miami-Dade
items.text:
NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE, FLA. (WSVN) - A man said that he was bitten by a dog after an incident in Northwest Miami-Dade.
The incident took place on Northwest 116th Street on Sunday morning.
The man shared his frustration afterward, and said that it was not the first time it occurred in the area.
“This is like the fifth time it happens, the dogs in front of my house. They are like dangerous dogs, they always leave them alone, they open the door, four people they’ve bitten on the street,” he said.
7News cameras captured a Miami-Dade Fire Rescue truck as well as police at the scene.
The circumstances behind the attack are unknown as of Sunday morning.
Please check back on WSVN.com and 7News for more details on this developing story.

items.title: The Miami Business Club’s first annual gala: Connections beyond just business
items.text:
On Oct. 10, the Miami Business Club took over the Miami Beach Convention Center for a night of entertainment, 1920s music and bond-building with business professionals around the Miami area.
The Miami Business Club was developed in 2020 by Stefan Lingmerth , an entrepreneur and investor who created Sunshine Kapital, a registered broker-dealer.
Their mission , according to their website, is to “drive the growth of our community forward and continue shaping a thriving future for South Florida.”
“The point of founding it was really to create a strong local business community,have good connections and have fun doing it, too. Just building that community, not really networking, I would say,” says Lingmerth.
Celebrating the successes of the MBC over the past six years, the event focused on the vast growth of membership in the organization.
A philanthropic focus to raise money for the Miami Waterkeeper was a key aspect of the event, prioritizing preservation of our natural waters and everything they have to offer the Miami area.
“The goal of the Miami Waterkeeper is to preserve and advocate for Miami’s waterways, particularly in Key Biscayne, and we’re also going up to Broward and Fort-Lauderdale,” said one of the Miami Waterkeeper representatives at the event.
Celebrating the connections built over the years, the event hosted hundreds of attendees and members of the MBC, from investors to content creators and tech workers to business owners.
The first two hours of the evening featured a mingling session outside of the Sunset Vista Ballroom for individuals to bond not solely over their work, but their lives and goals as well.
The area was precisely decorated with a red carpet for guests to be photographed, a balloon arch in red, cream, and gold, 1920s styled dancers tracing the room, and art pieces being sold at auction, created by Polen Cerci.
Guests could step out onto the balcony to overlook the city as the sun set throughout the evening.
The room was made up of people enjoying each other’s company, with laughter, conversation, and the recorded sound of Michael Buble filling the space.
“This is our inaugural, our first gala; the idea is to make it a marquee event that everyone wants to come to and everyone wants to participate in. We’re gonna have fun, and we’re gonna give back,” says Lingmerth.
“We have Miami Waterkeeper as our charity, so hopefully people donate, buy raffle tickets, bid on the auction, and we have the local business community that donated products and services to the auction.”
The event celebrated various business leaders within the club, including UM student Christian Yeagley, who was given the “Rookie of the Year” award for his success in developing his Influence Miami Magazine.
Keynote speakers included current Miami Beach governor Steven Meiner, who spoke about his first time attending a Miami Business Club meeting, and expressed how he continued to come to many meetings after and has deep support for the organization.
Alongside Governor Meiner, CEO of the Miami Waterkeeper, Rachel Silverstein spoke about the importance of our Miami waters and the value of donating to the organization.
In her words, “Without the bay, we are nothing.” The gala had frequent intermissions with various forms of entertainment between speakers, with performances from singer Julies, contortionist Elena Lee and dancing from the Peter London Global Dance Company.
